title: Copilot in a Teams meeting: availability modes
text: The meeting organizer controls the Allow Copilot and Facilitator option, subject to organization policy. The choices are During and after the meeting, Only during the meeting, and Off. In During and after mode, transcription is required for Copilot to use meeting speech. In Only during mode, Copilot can start from the meeting controls without transcription. If transcription starts, Copilot can be used during and after the meeting for the portions transcribed. If no transcript is started, untranscribed speech isn't available after the meeting and meeting-chat Copilot uses chat content only. If Allow Copilot is Off, live Copilot is unavailable and recording/transcription are disabled; meeting-chat Copilot can still be available for chat content only. Sensitivity labels and templates can also affect which option is available. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Copilot after a meeting and meeting recap
section: How to use Copilot after a meeting
text: To ask Copilot about spoken meeting content after the meeting, a meeting transcript must be available. Copilot can be opened from the meeting chat or Recap tab when the relevant meeting data is available. If Allow Copilot is Only during the meeting and no transcript was started, meeting-chat Copilot can use chat content only. If Allow Copilot is Off, meeting-chat Copilot can still be available for chat-only content. Check the meeting option and whether transcription actually ran before treating a missing post-meeting answer as a model failure. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Copilot in meetings hosted by another organization
section: How to use Copilot in a meeting
text: Microsoft Support states that Copilot will not work in a meeting hosted outside the participant's organization. When a user reports that the meeting Copilot control is unavailable, ask which organization hosted the meeting before investigating local client problems. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Meeting option controls for Copilot and Facilitator
text: The meeting option Allow Copilot and Facilitator determines when Copilot can be used during or after a meeting. In Only during the meeting mode, Copilot can work without transcription; when transcription is on, Copilot can also be used after the meeting for the transcribed content. Facilitator is available when Copilot is enabled. An organizer's default meeting options may be set by IT policy. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Organization policy for Copilot in Teams meetings
section: Manage Copilot for Teams meetings and events
text: Teams administrators can manage Copilot meeting defaults in the Teams admin center or with PowerShell. Policy values include On, On with saved transcript required, On with transcript saved by default, and Off. The policy affects the default and, depending on the selected value, whether an organizer can change the meeting-level setting. If the meeting option is missing or forced, ask an administrator to check the organizer's assigned meeting policy. This assistant only identifies the admin check; it does not change tenant settings. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Copilot without transcription or recording
text: Copilot can be configured for use only during a meeting without recording or saving a transcript. The organizer's meeting setting and organization policy determine whether that mode is available. External participants cannot interact with Copilot in this mode because Copilot cannot access external speech-to-text data. Multi-tenant organization participants can also be treated as external for this scenario. Check the meeting mode and participant's relationship to the host organization. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Intelligent recap without transcription
text: Intelligent recap without transcription can generate an AI summary after a scheduled meeting without saving a transcript or recording. The organizer must leave Intelligent recap turned on at the meeting's conclusion; the summary is available to attendees with Microsoft Copilot licenses after the scheduled meeting ends for everyone. The no-transcription recap path isn't supported for instant meetings. This is separate from standard post-meeting Copilot questions about spoken content, which require a transcript. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Meeting Recaps app and license prerequisites
text: The Meeting Recaps app can show recap material available to the signed-in user. Intelligent recap features require either a Microsoft Copilot license or a Teams Premium license. Audio and video recaps require a Microsoft Copilot license. Users without those licenses may still access recordings or transcripts when they have permission. If recap content is absent, distinguish license eligibility from the user's access permissions to the meeting artifacts. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Facilitator: supported meeting types and license
section: Add Facilitator to a meeting when scheduling
text: A Microsoft Copilot license is required to add Facilitator to a meeting or turn it on during a meeting. Facilitator can be added only to scheduled meetings; Microsoft Support says it cannot be added to channel meetings, instant meetings, or Teams calls. When the control is unavailable, first confirm the meeting type and then ask an administrator to verify the assigned license and policy. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Facilitator: who can turn it on during a meeting
text: Only meeting participants who are organizers or presenters and use Teams for web or desktop can turn Facilitator on or off during a meeting. Mobile participants can see live notes but cannot toggle Facilitator. If a user cannot see the control, check their meeting role and client platform before escalating a configuration issue. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Facilitator after the meeting and transcription
text: To prompt Facilitator about the meeting after it ends, transcription must have been turned on before or during the meeting. If Copilot is configured to start without transcription, Facilitator also starts without transcription. Generated notes may take a few minutes to appear because they are based on discussion captured in the transcript. Check transcription and allow time for notes to populate before reporting a failure. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Facilitator cannot find the agenda
section: Create an agenda for the meeting
text: Facilitator looks for an agenda in the meeting description or the Loop meeting notes component. If only the organizer has joined, Facilitator cannot read the organizer's copy of the meeting invite; the agenda can become available after a non-organizer joins. Facilitator also cannot read or extract an agenda from encrypted or sensitivity-labeled invite or notes content. These are documented behavior limits to check before treating agenda extraction as a service fault. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Interpreter: unsupported meeting types
text: Interpreter isn't currently supported in ad-hoc meetings, meetings using Microsoft Teams Rooms with personal devices, town halls, webinars, or Teams Free meetings. When the Interpreter control is absent, establish the meeting type and device arrangement first. If the scenario is unsupported, explain the limitation and don't recommend changing unrelated tenant settings. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Interpreter: supported calls
text: Interpreter in calls is supported only in one-to-one Teams-to-Teams VoIP calls. It is not supported in Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) calls. For call scenarios, ask whether the call is a direct Teams VoIP call or a PSTN call before troubleshooting meeting controls or licensing. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Interpreter: available interpretation languages
text: The Interpreter article lists English, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese, Simplified Chinese (Mandarin), Italian, German, French, Korean, and Taiwanese as supported interpretation output languages. Some spoken languages may be recognized without guaranteed interpretation accuracy. Output is limited to the supported languages listed in the article. Confirm both the spoken and target language when the user reports missing or unexpected translation. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Interpreter: transcript and recording behavior
text: Teams meeting recordings contain the original meeting audio, not the interpretation audio. Translated transcripts are available live during the meeting; after the meeting ends, the transcript shows the original spoken language. Interpreter may lag behind rapid exchanges, interruptions, or overlapping dialogue, and names or technical terms may be interpreted inaccurately. These are documented limitations rather than evidence of an access problem. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Interpreter: license and monthly usage checks
text: Microsoft Learn lists an eligible Microsoft 365 base license, an eligible Teams license, and a Microsoft Copilot license as prerequisites for Interpreter. For Teams Rooms devices, a Teams Rooms Pro license is required in place of the Copilot license. A Microsoft 365 license is required to listen to other participants' speech. Copilot and Teams Rooms Pro include 20 hours of interpretation per user per month; access beyond those hours is subject to available capacity. Ask an administrator to verify the user's actual license and device context. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.

title: Interpreter: external participants
text: Microsoft Support says people from other organizations can use Interpreter when they join from verified Microsoft 365 accounts with valid Microsoft Copilot licenses. Anonymous participants and guests cannot use Interpreter when their identity and license status cannot be verified. For external-participant problems, check the join identity and account type. Source reviewed 2026-10-30.
